correctness.rationale: For a fixed path, the forest-completion count is the principal Laplacian minor det(nI_r-J_r)=s n^(r-1) (or 1 for r=0); nonpath leaves and path endpoint leaves have separately proved exact deletion probabilities, yielding the conditional expectation without independence assumptions. Algebra determines all consecutive signs including last boundary, and g(k) is strictly increasing. The expansion is uniform at the cubic-root threshold. Prüfer-code enumeration 280392 trees, 35 determinant examples and 11026 exact transition checks passed from actual standalone checker; finite checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Full text of the closest Wiener-index/mixed-path-moment paper (2003) and of the distance-profile/leaf-bias paper (2021) was compared at the level of exact mathematical implications. Their published results do not specify the conditional global leaf-count regression at each distance or its sharp cubic mode; leaf-count marginal work and earlier Zagreb–Wiener mixed moments likewise do not imply this vector of means. Targeted semantic and open literature searches found no statement-level match; the remaining possible older joint enumerator is explicitly disclosed.

value.rationale: Leaf count measures local extremity/branching whereas fixed-pair distance is the elementary tree metric observable. The all-size exact regression has a nonmonotone shape with a cubic-root maximizing distance, a sharp integer threshold and infinitely many exact tie sizes, contrasting with sqrt(n) typical distances. The finite maximal advantage tends to 1/e and exposes a subtle O(1) dependence rather than a marginal or arbitrary slice. Its modest absolute magnitude and restricted model are disclosed.
